label: Kidney cancer (adult renal cell carcinoma)

approval.note: Draft checklist from NCG Guidelines for Urological Malignancies (2019): needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records transcribed from the NCG Guidelines for Urological Malignancies (2019) (National Cancer Grid, India), the renal cell carcinoma pages (investigations p 4, the pathways p 5 and 6, the pathology format p 61 to 63), each with its verbatim quote and page. Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' or 'proposal' (clinical_history) are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). A record NCG gives only under a condition the system never judges (an age, a finding, a plan) is shown with NCG's own tier and the condition, never counted. Adult renal cell carcinoma only: paediatric renal tumours (Wilms) are in another book. The book says routine renal mass biopsy is not indicated (p 4); the biopsy record is shown, not counted, in the localised setting. The stage and the risk group are as recorded by the clinician, never computed. Nothing here suggests treatment.
settings_note: Setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes stage). The two settings follow the book's pathways: 'Treatment pathway for localized disease' (p 5) and 'Treatment pathway for metastatic disease' (p 6).

records.tier_basis: No letter; proposed a. Performance status and comorbidity are recorded because the localised pathway names them (p 5 "poor Performance status, significant comorbidity")
